mainTopic: Selling פסולי המוקדשין and מעשר בהמה: the הקדש's gain at פדיון, orphans' tithe, הבלעה, and quoting a teaching in its author's name
overview: The משנה said that פסולי המוקדשין may be sold and slaughtered in the butcher market because 'their benefit goes to the הקדש.' The גמרא rules out a sale before פדיון, since a sanctified animal needs העמדה והערכה while alive. It concludes that the sale happens after פדיון. The הקדש gains because the owner, knowing he may sell the meat in the market, pays more to redeem it. Next the גמרא asks how a מעשר בהמה could be sold even at home, since a ברייתא says it is never sold. רב ששת answers that the משנה means orphans' מעשר בהמה, which the חכמים allowed to be sold to prevent their loss. A short story follows: רב ששת was upset when his teaching was repeated without his name, because a scholar's lips move in the grave when he is quoted. Back to the הלכה, אביי and רבא argue over the ברייתא about selling orphans' and adults' מעשר בהמה by הבלעה. רבא brings a פסוק showing that the ban on selling after שחיטה is only rabbinic.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה and asking when it applies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that the benefit from פסולי המוקדשין goes to the הקדש, and asks at what stage this is true.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: all disqualified consecrated animals, their benefit goes to the הקדש. When is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks a simple question: at what point in time is this true? This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished קרבן goes through two stages: first it still belongs to the הקדש, then the owner redeems it (פדיון). The גמרא wants to know which stage the משנה means when it says the 'benefit' goes to the הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated animals that became unfit for the מזבח (usually through a blemish) and are redeemed
Their benefit, meaning the money or profit that comes from them
The Temple treasury, or property belonging to it
When? At what stage?

phrases.english: GEMARA: All disqualified consecrated animals
their benefit goes to the Temple treasury.
When?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: At what stage (before or after פדיון) does the הקדש receive the benefit of פסולי המוקדשין?

steps.title: It cannot mean after redemption
steps.stepSummary: If the sale happens after פדיון, the money belongs to the owner, not to the הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means after it was redeemed, does the benefit go to the הקדש? The benefit belongs to the owners!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option, that the משנה is talking about after פדיון, and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the owner redeems the animal, it is his regular property. Any money he makes selling it in the market is his own. So the words 'its benefit goes to the הקדש' cannot describe a sale after פדיון.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject)
Redemption: buying the animal back from the הקדש so it becomes ordinary
The owners

phrases.english: If you say after its redemption
does their benefit go to the Temple treasury?
Their benefit belongs to the owners!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the משנה refers to a sale after פדיון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After פדיון the animal belongs to the owner, so any profit is his and not the הקדש's.

steps.title: Suggesting it means before redemption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the משנה refers to before פדיון, when the money still goes to the הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means before its redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: Since 'after redemption' failed, the גמרא tries the other option: before פדיון. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before פדיון the animal still belongs to the הקדש, so money paid for it would go to the הקדש. That fits the words 'הנאתן להקדש' well.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (brings in a new suggestion after the old one failed)

phrases.english: Rather, before its redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the other option after step 2 rejected 'after פדיון'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה refers to a sale before פדיון, when the proceeds go to the הקדש.

steps.title: Before redemption it cannot be slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: Before פדיון the animal must be stood up and valued alive, so how could the משנה allow it to be slaughtered in the market first?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can they be slaughtered? But it needs standing and valuation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'before redemption' idea. The משנה allows slaughtering in the market, but an animal that has not yet been redeemed must first be valued while alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To redeem a sanctified animal, it has to be stood before a כהן so he can set its value (העמדה והערכה). That can only happen while it is alive. So if the animal is slaughtered before פדיון, it can no longer be redeemed properly. This clashes with the משנה's word 'נשחטין'.

keyTerms.meaning: They are slaughtered (the משנה's word about slaughtering in the butcher market)
Standing: placing the live animal before a כהן
Valuation: the כהן setting its price

steps.confusionAlert: 'נשחטין' is not a new ruling. The גמרא is quoting the משנה's own word and asking how it fits with the 'before redemption' idea.

phrases.english: Are they slaughtered?
But it requires standing and valuation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the משנה refers to before פדיון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redemption requires a live animal to be stood and valued, so it cannot be slaughtered before פדיון, yet the משנה says it is slaughtered.

steps.title: The problem only works away for one opinion
steps.stepSummary: If קדשי מזבח do not need העמדה והערכה, there is no problem. But for the view that they do, the difficulty stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says that items consecrated for the altar were not included in standing and valuation. But for the one who says they were included in standing and valuation, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that the challenge in step 4 can be avoided according to one opinion. It cannot be avoided according to the other, so the 'before redemption' approach still does not work for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a dispute whether animals consecrated for the מזבח need העמדה והערכה. If they do not, the animal could be slaughtered first and redeemed afterward, so 'before redemption' would be fine. Since the other opinion does require it, the גמרא needs an explanation of the משנה that works for both views.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well according to the one who says
Items consecrated to be offered on the altar
Included in
What is there to say? (the difficulty remains)

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
items consecrated for the altar were not
included in standing and valuation,
but according to the one who says
they were included in standing and valuation,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the difficulty of step 4 can only be avoided according to one opinion, so it stands overall.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'before redemption' reading of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reading only works for the view that קדשי מזבח need no העמדה והערכה, so it fails for the opposing view.

steps.title: It really is after redemption: the הקדש gains at the start
steps.stepSummary: The sale happens after פדיון. 'הנאתן להקדש' refers to the gain the הקדש gets at the original redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it really is after redemption. And what does 'their benefit goes to the הקדש' mean? At the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to 'after redemption' and reinterprets the משנה's phrase. The benefit to the הקדש is not the market profit. It is something that happens at the start, at the time of פדיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the slaughtering happens after פדיון, so העמדה והערכה is no longer a problem. The earlier objection (the profit belongs to the owner) is answered too, because the הקדש's 'benefit' happens back at the redemption, not at the market sale. Since the redeemed animal may be sold like regular meat, it is worth more, so the הקדש receives a higher redemption price.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (going back to an earlier option)
And what does it mean? (reinterprets a phrase)
At the beginning: referring to the original redemption

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's sale and slaughter happen after פדיון. 'הנאתן להקדש' means the הקדש benefits at the initial redemption, not from the later market sale.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the משנה allows only פסולי המוקדשין to be sold in the market. Doing so helps the הקדש at the time of redemption, which is not true of a בכור or מעשר, whose benefit goes to the owner.

phrases.english: Rather, it is actually after redemption,
and what is meant by 'their benefit goes to the Temple treasury'?
It refers to the beginning.
phrases.notes: He means the first redemption from the הקדש, before the animal was ever sold in the market.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the 'after redemption' option rejected in step 2 and solves its problem by reinterpreting the phrase.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הנאתן להקדש' meant the profit from the market sale goes to the הקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sale is after פדיון. 'הנאתן להקדש' refers to the הקדש's gain at the initial redemption.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The animals are sold and slaughtered after פדיון, avoiding the need for העמדה והערכה, and the הקדש benefits at the time of the original redemption.

steps.title: Market sale makes the owner pay more at redemption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how the הקדש gains: the owner knows he can sell the meat at full market value, so he redeems it for more money from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה allows these redeemed animals to be sold in the market, slaughtered in the market, and weighed by the litra, the owner will pay more to redeem them in the first place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the answer from step 6. It explains exactly how the הקדש benefits from the market sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sale itself happens after פדיון, so the money from the sale goes to the owner. But because the owner expects to sell the meat at the best price, he is willing to pay a higher price at the פדיון. That higher price is the gain that goes to the הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: The butchers' market
A litra, a unit of weight used to sell meat
Redeems
At the start, from the beginning

steps.whatToRemember: 'הנאתן להקדש' does not mean the sale money goes to the הקדש. It means the הקדש gets a higher redemption price, because a market sale is allowed later.

phrases.english: For since the Master permits them
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here means the תנא of our משנה.

phrases.english: to be sold in the butchers' market
and slaughtered in the butchers' market
and weighed by the litra
he redeems it for more at the start

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the answer in step 6 works
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the mechanism: the gain is indirect, through a higher redemption price
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gain to the הקדש would have to come from the money of the market sale itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The gain to the הקדש comes from the higher price the owner pays at פדיון, because he knows he may sell the meat in the market later.

steps.title: Can a tithe animal be sold even at home?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's exception for בכור and מעשר. It asks how a מעשר בהמה could be sold at home at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: except for the בכור and the מעשר, whose benefit goes to the owner. It makes sense for a בכור: it may not be sold in the market, but it may be sold at home. But a מעשר: may it be sold at home?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה. It points out a problem with the מעשר part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to say that a בכור and a מעשר only lose the right to be sold in the market, so selling at home should be fine. For a בכור that works. For a מעשר בהמה, the גמרא doubts that any sale is allowed, even at home.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal, given to a כהן
Animal tithe: every tenth animal, which is holy
The owner
Granted, this part makes sense

phrases.english: Except for the firstborn and the tithe
whose benefit goes to the owner.
Granted, a firstborn:
it is in the market that it may not be sold,
but in his house it may be sold.
But a tithe animal:
may it be sold in his house?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּכוֹר בָּאִיטְלִיז הוּא דְּלָא מִיזְדַּבַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's suggestion that a מעשר בהמה may be sold at home
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה only bans selling in the market. That suggests a home sale is allowed, but a מעשר בהמה may not be sold at all.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a tithe animal is never sold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as proof for its question: a בכור may be sold alive, but a מעשר בהמה may never be sold in any condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: for a בכור the Torah says 'You shall not redeem', and it may be sold alive. For a מעשר the Torah says 'It shall not be redeemed', and it may not be sold: not alive and not slaughtered, not unblemished and not blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its question from step 8 with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says clearly that a מעשר בהמה can never be sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the two animals differently. A בכור may be sold, but a מעשר בהמה may not be sold in any condition, even when slaughtered or blemished. This seems to go against the משנה, which suggests a home sale of a blemished מעשר בהמה is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a challenge from a ברייתא)
'You shall not redeem', said about a בכור
'It shall not be redeemed', said about מעשר
An unblemished animal
A blemished animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two פסוקים. Both say the animal cannot be redeemed. The difference is that a בכור may still be sold alive, but a מעשר בהמה may not be sold at all.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Regarding a firstborn it says: 'You shall not redeem'
and it may be sold alive;
regarding the tithe it says: 'It shall not be redeemed'
and it may not be sold,
not alive and not slaughtered,
not unblemished and not blemished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the question in step 8
steps.raayaObject: That a מעשר בהמה may not be sold even at home
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads the פסוק 'לא יגאל' as banning any sale of מעשר בהמה

steps.title: רב ששת: the tithe animal of orphans
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the משנה means a מעשר בהמה belonging to orphans. The חכמים allowed its sale so the orphans would not lose money.
steps.simpleTranslation: This question troubled רב ששת at night, and he solved it in the morning from a ברייתא: we are dealing with the מעשר בהמה of orphans. The חכמים made an allowance for it because of השבת אבידה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question from steps 8 and 9. He says the משנה is talking about a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule from the ברייתא still stands: a מעשר בהמה is not sold. The משנה describes an exception for young orphans, who cannot eat all the meat and would lose it. To prevent that loss, the חכמים allowed a sale, treating it like returning a lost item.

keyTerms.meaning: At night
In the morning
We are dealing with (a specific case)
Orphans
Returning a lost item; here, preventing someone's loss

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on selling מעשר בהמה stays in place. The משנה's home sale is an exception for orphans, so they will not lose money.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the חכמים making a special allowance inside a strict rule, to protect people who cannot protect themselves.

phrases.english: This matter was difficult for
רב ששת at night,
and he resolved it in the morning from a ברייתא:
we are dealing with the animal tithe of orphans,
and because of returning a lost item they touched upon it.
phrases.notes: 'They touched upon it' means the חכמים made a special allowance to let it be sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִילְּתָא אִיקַּשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּאוּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in steps 8 and 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a special case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה allows any owner to sell a blemished מעשר בהמה at home, which goes against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about orphans' מעשר בהמה. The חכמים allowed its sale to prevent the orphans' loss, while the general ban stays in place.

steps.title: רב ששת's attendant repeats his teaching without credit
steps.stepSummary: רבי אידי heard רב ששת's answer and repeated it in the בית מדרש without saying whose it was. רב ששת was upset and said: let the one who stung me be stung by a scorpion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אידי, רב ששת's attendant, heard this answer from him. He went and said it in the study hall, but not in רב ששת's name. רב ששת heard and was annoyed. He said: Whoever stung me, let a scorpion sting him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the הלכה to tell a short story about רב ששת's answer from the last step. His attendant shared it without giving him credit, and רב ששת was hurt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the story is that quoting a teaching without naming its author is a real wrong. רב ששת felt 'stung', and this sets up the question of why it mattered so much to him.

keyTerms.meaning: His attendant, the student who served him
The study hall
In his name, giving him credit
He was annoyed or upset
A scorpion

phrases.english: Rabbi Idi, the attendant of Rav Sheshet,
heard it from him.
phrases.notes: 'It' is רב ששת's answer from the last step, that the משנה means orphans' מעשר בהמה.

phrases.english: He went and said it in the study hall,
but did not say it in his name.
Rav Sheshet heard and was annoyed.
He said: The one who stung me,
let a scorpion sting him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אִידִי סַרְסְיֵהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת הֲוָה שַׁמְעַהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story about how רב ששת's answer from step 10 was passed on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeating a teaching without crediting its author caused רב ששת real distress.

steps.title: Why did it matter to רב ששת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference it made to רב ששת whether his name was mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רב ששת, what difference did it make to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: why should רב ששת care, as long as the Torah is being taught? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think a great scholar would not care about credit. The גמרא wants to show there is a real spiritual reason for being quoted, not just pride.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make to him?

phrases.english: And as for Rav Sheshet,
what difference does it make to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת מַאי נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the reason behind רב ששת's reaction in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why being quoted by name mattered to רב ששת.

steps.title: David asked to be quoted in this world
steps.stepSummary: רב reads the פסוק 'I will dwell in Your tent forever (עולמים, worlds)' as דוד's request to be quoted in this world after he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: What does the פסוק 'I will dwell in Your tent for worlds' mean? Can a person live in two worlds at once? Rather, דוד said: Master of the world, let people say a teaching in my name in this world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a teaching of רב about a פסוק in תהלים. It shows that even דוד המלך wanted his Torah repeated in his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עולמים is plural, which seems to mean living in two worlds at once, and that is impossible. So רב explains: while דוד is in the next world, he 'lives' in this world too, through people quoting his Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: I will dwell in Your tent forever (literally, 'for worlds')
Master of the world, a way of speaking to ה'
A teaching of Torah or halacha
This world

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'I will dwell in Your tent forever'?
phrases.notes: תהלים 61:5. עולמים literally means 'worlds', in the plural.

phrases.english: Is it possible for a person
to live in two worlds?
Rather, David said:
Master of the world,
let them say a teaching
from my mouth in this world.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Being quoted in this world after death is something even דוד המלך asked for, so it really matters.

steps.title: A scholar's lips move in the grave
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, explains why being quoted matters: when a תלמיד חכם is quoted in this world, his lips move in the grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: Any תלמיד חכם who is quoted on a teaching in this world, his lips move in the grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up דוד's request with a teaching from רבי שמעון בן יוחי. It explains what a scholar gains when he is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being quoted is not about fame. It keeps the scholar 'speaking' even after death, so leaving out his name takes away something real.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar
Move gently, as if speaking
In the grave

steps.whatToRemember: When you say a Torah teaching in the name of the one who said it, his lips move in the grave. That is why רב ששת was so upset.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
Any Torah scholar
whom people quote on a teaching
from his mouth in this world,
his lips move in the grave.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why דוד wanted to be quoted, as stated in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: Why being quoted in this world benefits a scholar who has died.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי.

steps.title: The verse: lips moving like a pile of grapes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר זעירי brings the פסוק from שיר השירים, 'moving the lips of those asleep'. A pile of grapes drips when touched, and a scholar's lips move when he is quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר זעירי said: What is the source? 'And your mouth is like the best wine... moving the lips of those who are asleep.' It is like a pile of grapes: when a person touches it, it drips. So too with Torah scholars: when someone says a teaching in their name, their lips move in the grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק that is the source for the idea in the last step. It compares a scholar's lips to a pile of ripe grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Those who are asleep' are the dead, and 'moving their lips' is the same word, דובב, used by רבי שמעון בן יוחי. The grape picture shows that just a light touch, a quote, sets the lips moving.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק that teaches this?
A pile of ripe grapes, left warm before pressing
Those who are asleep, here meaning the dead

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak bar Zeiri said:
What is the verse that teaches it?
'And your mouth is like the best wine,
that goes down smoothly for my beloved,
moving the lips of those who are asleep.'
Like a pile of grapes.
Just as a pile of grapes,
once a person touches it, it drips,
so too Torah scholars:
once a person says
a teaching in his name,
his lips move in the grave.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר זְעֵירִי מַאי קְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבי שמעון בן יוחי's teaching in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That a scholar's lips move in the grave when he is quoted.

steps.title: Which ברייתא did רב ששת rely on?
steps.stepSummary: Back to the הלכה: the גמרא asks which ברייתא is behind רב ששת's answer about orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and the גמרא goes back to רב ששת's answer from step 10. It asks for the ברייתא behind it, and the next step will quote it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said that orphans' מעשר בהמה may be sold. The גמרא now wants the written source that teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: What is the baraita?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of steps 11–15 and goes back to the הלכה of step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of the ברייתא behind רב ששת's answer.

steps.title: The ברייתא: orphans' tithe animal may be sold
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says orphans' מעשר בהמה may be sold. Also, after a מעשר בהמה is slaughtered, its meat's price may be folded into the price of its hide, fat, sinews and horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Orphans' מעשר בהמה may be sold. And if a person slaughtered a מעשר בהמה, he may fold the meat's price into the price of its hide, its fat, its sinews and its horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא. It backs up רב ששת's answer that orphans' מעשר בהמה may be sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a מעשר בהמה may not be sold at all. For orphans the חכמים made an exception so they would not lose money. The second rule gives another way around the ban: the meat itself is not sold, but its value is added to the price of the parts that may be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans
He folds it in, adding its value into another price
Its hide
Its sinews

steps.whatToRemember: מעשר בהמה usually cannot be sold. Orphans' animals are an exception, and the meat's value can also be folded into the price of the parts that may be sold.
steps.confusionAlert: The meat itself is still not being sold. Only the hide, fat, sinews and horns are sold, at a higher price that covers the meat's value.

phrases.english: As it was taught: An animal tithe belonging to orphans,
may be sold.
And an animal tithe that he slaughtered,
he folds its value into its hide,
phrases.notes: He adds the meat's price onto the price of these parts, which may be sold.

phrases.english: its fat, its sinews, and its horns.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה שֶׁל יְתוֹמִים מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא allows selling orphans' מעשר בהמה, and allows folding a slaughtered מעשר's meat value into the price of its sellable parts.

steps.title: What is the ברייתא really saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to read the ברייתא about orphans' מעשר בהמה, since it seems to say two different things.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the ברייתא saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the ברייתא it just quoted. This sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first says the orphans' animal may simply be sold. Then it talks about folding the meat's price into the price of the hide and other parts. Is that one rule or two? The גמרא wants to know.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? A request to explain unclear wording
The tenth animal of the flock, which is holy

phrases.english: What is it saying?
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from the last step. It seems to allow a normal sale, and then also talks about folding in the price.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the ברייתא quoted in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא gives two separate rules (plain sale, and sale by folding in) or one combined rule.

steps.title: אביי: orphans may sell it only by folding in the price
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא gives one rule: an orphans' מעשר בהמה may be sold, but only through הבלעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what it means: an orphans' מעשר בהמה may be sold, but only by folding its price into the price of other things.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. The two parts of the ברייתא are really one rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'it may be sold' are not a separate, open permission. The sale is allowed only by הבלעה. The buyer pays a high price for the hide, fat, sinews and horns, and that price quietly covers the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Folding one item's price into the price of another item
Orphans
This is what it means. Introduces an explanation of a text

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it is saying:
An animal tithe of orphans
is sold by inclusion.
phrases.notes: 'Inclusion' means the meat's price is hidden inside the price of the hide and other parts, as in step 17.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is one rule: orphans' מעשר בהמה may be sold, but only by הבלעה.

steps.title: So an adult may not sell it even by folding in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from אביי's reading that an adult (non-orphan) may not sell the meat of his מעשר בהמה, even by הבלעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that an adult may not sell it, even by folding in the price.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from אביי's explanation. This conclusion sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Folding in the price was allowed only as a special leniency for orphans. So for an ordinary adult owner, even this indirect sale is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; we can infer from this
An adult, here an owner who is not an orphan

phrases.english: By implication, that an adult's
phrases.notes: 'Adult' here means a regular owner who is not an orphan.

phrases.english: may not be sold even by inclusion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from אביי's answer in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An adult's מעשר בהמה may not be sold, even by הבלעה.

steps.title: But folding in is allowed for a לולב and אתרוג in שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference using the case of buying a לולב in שביעית. There רב הונא lets the seller fold the אתרוג's price into the לולב's price.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from what was taught: Someone who buys a לולב from his friend in שביעית is given an אתרוג as a gift, because he may not buy it in שביעית. We asked: if the seller does not want to give it as a gift, what then? רב הונא said: he folds the אתרוג's price into the price of the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that an adult may not use הבלעה. It points to another case where folding in the price is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שביעית the אתרוג may not be bought directly, yet רב הונא allows hiding its price inside the לולב's price. So why not allow an adult to hide the meat's price inside the hide's price too?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? Introduces a contradiction
The seventh, sabbatical year
The palm branch used on סוכות
The citron used on סוכות
And we discussed it. Brings up an earlier discussion

phrases.english: What is different from that which is taught:
One who buys a lulav from his friend in the Sabbatical Year
he gives him an etrog as a gift,
because he is not permitted
to buy it in the Sabbatical Year.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the אתרוג. The לולב may be bought, but the אתרוג may not.

phrases.english: And we discussed it:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רָצָה לִיתֵּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה מַאי?
phrases.english: If he did not want to give it to him as a gift, what then?
And Rav Huna said:
He includes the price of the etrog in the lulav!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 20 from a similar case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that an adult may not sell his מעשר בהמה even by הבלעה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא allows הבלעה for an אתרוג that may not be sold directly in שביעית. So הבלעה should also be allowed for an adult's מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: With the אתרוג the trick is hidden, with the meat it is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: folding the אתרוג's price into the לולב's price is not noticeable, but folding the meat's price into the hide and horns is plain to see.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the matter is not obvious. Here, the matter is obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing a difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לולב's price can go up and down, so a higher price does not look strange. But hide, fat, sinews and horns are worth little, so a big price for them clearly means the buyer is paying for the meat. Since the trick is obvious, an adult may not use it.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in the other case
Here, in our case
The matter is obvious; it is plain to see

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, an orphans' מעשר בהמה may be sold only by הבלעה, and an adult's may not be sold even that way, because here the folded-in price is obvious, unlike the אתרוג folded into the לולב. The next step shows רבא rejecting this reading.

phrases.english: There, the matter is not evident,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the לולב and אתרוג. A higher לולב price does not stand out.

phrases.english: here, the matter is evident.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא מוֹכְחָא מִילְּתָא, הָכָא מוֹכְחָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since הבלעה works for the אתרוג, it should work for an adult's מעשר בהמה too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Within אביי's reading, הבלעה is allowed only where it is not obvious. With the animal's cheap parts it is obvious, so an adult may not use it, and only orphans got a special leniency. רבא goes on to read the ברייתא differently.

steps.title: רבא asks why the phrase appears twice
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי: if the ברייתא is only one case, why does it say 'מעשר בהמה' twice?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If so, why do I need the words 'animal tithe' two times?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's reading of the ברייתא from Step 19. He points out that the words 'מעשר בהמה' appear twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי read the ברייתא as one rule about orphans. If that were right, saying 'מעשר בהמה' once would be enough. The repeated phrase suggests the ברייתא is describing two separate cases.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, meaning if your reading is right
Two times
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: Rava said: If so,
why do I need "animal tithe" two times?

steps.triggerLanguage: אם כן מעשר בהמה תרי זמני למה לי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to attack אביי's reading from Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's one-case reading of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A repeated phrase must mean something, so it points to two cases rather than one.

steps.title: רבא reads the ברייתא as two separate cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that orphans sell the meat normally, while an adult may sell it only through הבלעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said, this is what it means: orphans' animal tithe may be sold in the usual way. An adult's animal tithe that was slaughtered may be sold only by folding its price into the hide, fat, sinews and horns.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to the question from Step 18. Each mention of 'מעשר בהמה' in the ברייתא is a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For orphans, the meat may be sold openly with no trick needed. For a גדול, the sale has to be hidden inside the price of the other parts. This is the opposite of אביי's view, where even orphans needed הבלעה.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans (young heirs)
In its usual way, openly
An adult (not an orphan)
He folds its price into something else

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two views. For אביי, orphans need הבלעה and an adult may not sell at all. For רבא, orphans sell normally and an adult uses הבלעה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the law for both orphans and adults compared to אביי's reading.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
This is what it is saying:
An animal tithe belonging to orphans
may be sold in its usual way,
but an animal tithe of an adult that he slaughtered
he folds its price into its hide, its fat,
its sinews and its horns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new reading after rejecting אביי's
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two cases: orphans sell normally, and an adult sells by הבלעה.

steps.title: רבא brings a פסוק as his source
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks where his view comes from and quotes the פסוק about מעשר בהמה and its תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do I learn this? As it is written: "Then it and its substitute shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a פסוק to support his ruling that an adult's מעשר בהמה can be sold after שחיטה. The explanation of how the פסוק proves it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts תמורה and 'it shall not be redeemed' side by side. רבא will use that closeness to compare the two laws.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this?
A substitute animal that becomes holy in place of a קרבן
It shall not be redeemed (here, it may not be sold)

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say this?
As it is written:
"Then both it and its substitute
shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רבא's reading from Step 24
steps.raayaObject: That an adult may sell the meat after שחיטה (by הבלעה)

steps.title: Selling after slaughter is allowed by Torah law and banned by the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: Like תמורה, the ban on selling applies only while the animal is alive. After שחיטה, only a rabbinic גזירה forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does it make a substitute? While alive. When may it not be redeemed? While alive. So after slaughter it may be redeemed. It is the Rabbis who decreed against selling after slaughter, because people might come to sell before slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains how the פסוק proves his point. The selling ban is compared to תמורה, which only works while the animal is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two laws sit together in the פסוק, the selling ban also covers only a live animal. So by Torah law the meat may be sold after שחיטה. The ban after שחיטה is only a rabbinic fence, which is why הבלעה can be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: While the animal is alive
Redeemed, here meaning sold
They made a rabbinic decree
Because of the worry about

steps.whyThisMatters: Since the ban after שחיטה is only rabbinic, the Rabbis could allow ways around it such as הבלעה.

phrases.english: When does it make a substitute? While alive.
When may it not be redeemed? While alive.
phrases.notes: "Redeemed" here means sold, the way the פסוק was read earlier.

phrases.english: So after slaughter, it may be redeemed.
And it is the Rabbis who decreed
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: against selling after slaughter, because of selling before slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק from Step 25 proves the point
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law the meat may be sold after שחיטה. Only a rabbinic גזירה forbids it.

steps.title: The Rabbis' decree covers what is priced while alive
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts to limit the גזירה to parts of the animal that are valued while it is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: For an item that is priced while the animal is alive, the Rabbis decreed against selling after slaughter, because people might come to sell before slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins to narrow the rabbinic גזירה. This sentence sets up a contrast that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat is what gives a live animal its value, so selling the meat could be confused with selling the live animal. That is why the Rabbis made a גזירה about the meat. The other parts will be treated differently, and that difference is what makes הבלעה work.

keyTerms.meaning: An item that is priced or valued
The Rabbis decreed

phrases.english: An item that is priced while the animal is alive
phrases.notes: He means the meat, which is what a live animal is mainly valued for.

because of selling before slaughter,
